review_cost.rationale: Not approve-as-is: the two client-side races need a fix and re-review, and there are a few hygiene nits. But every change is small and localized in an otherwise idiomatic, well-layered codebase — one round, not rework.

findings.issue: applyFilters builds the next URL from home.value.filters (the async routeLoader signal), so changing a second filter — or typing during the debounce — while the first navigation's q-data.json is still in flight silently drops the earlier filter (type/generation vanish from the URL).
findings.suggestion: Derive the current q/type/generation from loc.url (useLocation().url.searchParams) or from dedicated signals, not from the loader value; the loader stays a pure projection of the URL.

findings.issue: The 200 ms search debounce timer is never cancelled when the home route unmounts; navigating away within the window fires applyFilters from the dead component and navigates the user back to '/?q=…'.
findings.suggestion: Clear the timer in a cleanup: useTask$(({ cleanup }) => { cleanup(() => clearTimeout(timer.value)) }) or an equivalent unmount hook.

findings.issue: The in-memory cache Map has no size cap or eviction policy; keys are only bounded by the API's URL space, and a permanently-hung refresh leaves refreshing=true forever (no retry).
findings.suggestion: Add a simple size cap/LRU and a refresh timeout, or reset hit.time when a refresh fails to start/complete.

findings.issue: fetchJson has no timeout or AbortSignal, so a hung upstream request stalls SSR (streaming never completes) with no error surfaced; a thrown loader currently yields a bare 500.
findings.suggestion: Pass AbortSignal.timeout(...) to fetch and add a graceful error state (or at least a log) for upstream failures.

findings.issue: An uncached Pokémon page fans out to one fetch per move plus one per version group (~100+ upstream requests); the 30 s SWR cache bounds it, but a cache stampede after expiry on a popular page is worth thinking about.
findings.suggestion: Consider caching the per-(game,method) resolved move rows, or deduplicating in-flight requests more aggressively (e.g. share the moveRow promise per name across requests).

findings.issue: One 400+ line module assembles data for all five page types; every route loader depends on it, making it the app's merge-conflict hotspot and the one file that must change for any new page.
findings.suggestion: Split per page (lib/pages/home.ts, pokemon.ts, …) keeping shared pieces (speciesById, mainTypes, cardsForPokemon) in a small lib/api-derived core.

findings.issue: Six unrelated components (TypeBadge, PokemonCard, CardList, Section, Evolution, NotFound) live in one grab-bag file.
findings.suggestion: One file per component (or small themed groups) so imports and ownership are obvious.

findings.issue: devDependency 'undici: *' is unused by any source file (Node's global fetch is used) and the '*' range makes installs non-deterministic.
findings.suggestion: Remove it; if it was needed for a specific fetch issue, pin it and leave a comment.

findings.issue: typesPage() calls mainTypes(), which fetches all 18 full type records (each large) when the page only needs names.
findings.suggestion: Have typesPage use the lighter list endpoint, or accept the cost explicitly given the 30 s cache.

findings.issue: Three mirrored signals plus a useTask$ re-sync duplicate the loader state so remove() can patch locally; workable but a second place where member/coverage state can drift from the loader.
findings.suggestion: Keep the loader result as the base and store only the client-side mutation (e.g. a 'removed' set) applied on top, or invalidate the loader after the cookie write.

summary: This is a genuinely idiomatic Qwik City 1.20 app — routeLoader$ for all data, URL-driven filters, official node adapter, 404 via status(), and a server/pure-client lib split that I verified actually holds in the built client bundle. What blocks approve-as-is is a pair of small client-side races on the home page (filter state read from the async loader value, and an uncleaned debounce timer), plus hygiene nits (unbounded cache, unused 'undici: *', monolithic data.ts). One round of localized fixes and I'd merge it.
